{
  "decision": {
    "mode": "commands",
    "questions": [],
    "commands": [
      {
        "warnings": [],
        "risk": "low",
        "title": "Identify the host distribution",
        "explanation": "Read the installed operating-system identity to check the reported Ubuntu environment against the compatibility failure. This does not change the host.",
        "requires_admin": false,
        "command": "cat /etc/os-release",
        "expected_result": "Distribution ID, release version and related compatibility identifiers."
      },
      {
        "warnings": [],
        "risk": "low",
        "title": "Check the host architecture",
        "explanation": "Read the kernel and machine architecture so a distribution mismatch can be distinguished from an architecture mismatch.",
        "requires_admin": false,
        "command": "uname -smr",
        "expected_result": "Kernel name, kernel release and machine architecture."
      },
      {
        "warnings": [],
        "risk": "low",
        "title": "Find currently failed service units",
        "explanation": "Check whether the demo failure corresponds to a failed system service. An empty list would not rule out a manually launched demo or a user service.",
        "requires_admin": false,
        "command": "systemctl --failed --no-pager --full",
        "expected_result": "Failed system units, or an indication that none are currently failed."
      },
      {
        "warnings": [],
        "risk": "low",
        "title": "Discover exact installed service names",
        "explanation": "List service definitions without guessing the demo's unit name. The captured results will allow subsequent inspection to target an exact unit rather than unrelated logs.",
        "requires_admin": false,
        "command": "systemctl list-unit-files --type=service --no-pager",
        "expected_result": "Installed service unit names and their enablement states, potentially across multiple automatically captured pages."
      },
      {
        "warnings": [
          "The inventory can span multiple automatically captured pages; no package is installed or changed."
        ],
        "risk": "low",
        "title": "Discover the installed demo package",
        "explanation": "Collect installed package names and versions to identify the actual demo package without assuming its name. If it is absent, investigate a manually installed or otherwise separately managed demo rather than assuming an APT repair is appropriate.",
        "requires_admin": false,
        "command": "apt list --installed",
        "expected_result": "Installed package names, versions and architectures for comparison with the host and reported compatibility error."
      }
    ]
  },
  "roadmap": [
    {
      "checks": [
        "Read distribution identity and architecture; compare them with the supplied Ubuntu 24.04 context.",
        "Discover exact service and package names from read-only inventories.",
        "Retain the already captured demo log; its compatibility message is a diagnostic lead, not independent proof of the root cause."
      ],
      "purpose": "Establish host facts and identify the affected component without changing the disposable environment.",
      "title": "1. Collect host and component evidence"
    },
    {
      "checks": [
        "After exact names are observed, inspect the matching unit's status, launch configuration, executable path and exit information.",
        "Collect logs scoped to that unit with explicit time and line limits and no pager.",
        "Inspect metadata for the observed package and compare version, architecture, dependencies and distribution provenance with host facts.",
        "If an inventory capture is incomplete, narrow subsequent queries to exact names visible in the captured evidence; do not infer missing entries.",
        "If no matching system unit or package exists, investigate user-service or standalone installation evidence before selecting a package manager."
      ],
      "purpose": "Determine whether the failure is genuinely a distribution mismatch, another compatibility issue, or a misleading application diagnostic. These targeted commands depend on the inventory results.",
      "title": "2. Confirm the failure mechanism"
    },
    {
      "checks": [
        "Identify the actual configuration and data locations before considering any changes.",
        "Preserve relevant configuration and an available recovery path before replacement or reconfiguration.",
        "Select a host-compatible supported build only after package provenance and host requirements are established.",
        "Do not reinstall, remove packages, change repositories, restart services or alter access settings merely because the log suggests incompatibility.",
        "If a repair requires unavailable credentials or a choice about replacing demo data, obtain that decision before proceeding."
      ],
      "purpose": "Choose the least disruptive response based on evidence; a documented diagnosis alone may satisfy the original goal.",
      "title": "3. Select a repair only if warranted"
    },
    {
      "checks": [
        "If an authorized repair is later performed, verify the resulting package metadata and service state independently.",
        "Collect fresh, bounded service logs and run the documented compatibility check only after its exact invocation and effects are known.",
        "Compare results with the original failure and report unresolved evidence explicitly.",
        "If validation fails, preserve new diagnostics and use the prepared recovery approach rather than repeating the change."
      ],
      "purpose": "Demonstrate whether the compatibility issue was resolved without claiming success from an idle prompt or capture marker.",
      "title": "4. Verify and summarize"
    }
  ],
  "explanation": "The captured log reports a distribution compatibility failure, but it does not yet establish the package identity or prove the cause. Replace the remaining identity check with these read-only diagnostics; targeted log collection and any repair must wait for their evidence. Commands are individually reviewable, and sending a command only types it—it does not press Enter.",
  "assumptions": [
    "The supplied target is Ubuntu 24.04 LTS with bash and local-console access; installed OS evidence will verify that context.",
    "The previously captured log is available and need not be read again at this stage.",
    "The demo package name, service name and installation method are not yet established.",
    "No administrative privileges or system changes are needed for this diagnostic phase."
  ]
}
